CORRECTION to the scope of this bead, from my own follow-up measurement.

I claimed the lowering cannot vary through any public path. That is wrong as stated. It is true only of the EFFECT-FORM path.

measurement_form() (R/evidence-api.R:230) is exported and takes reducer as a user-settable, validated parameter (default aggregate_first(), validated by .validate_partition_reducer). Passing reduce_partitions() instead produces a genuinely different plan:

  aggregate_first():   ordered_partition_product -> partition_sufficient_reduction ->
                       neural_feature_normalization -> edge_transform ->
                       experimental_projection -> effect_coupling_materialization
  reduce_partitions(): ordered_partition_product -> neural_feature_normalization ->
                       edge_transform -> partition_reduction ->
                       experimental_projection -> effect_coupling_materialization

Receipts differ (identical() FALSE). Numeric values are identical (max|diff| = 0) on a raw bilinear form, which is correct - reduction order commutes when no nonlinear edge transform is present, exactly as evidence-pairing-contract section 12 states. The axis is live and recorded, not cosmetic.

So aggregate_first and reduce_partitions are NOT dead exports, and neither is inner_product (used as the pinned default at compiler.R:76,147,429 and evidence-task.R:336). The genuinely unreachable set is narrower than I said: correlation(), cosine(), covariance() -> effect_edge_normalizer, and fisher_z(), rank_edges() -> effect_edge_transform. Their only evaluator, .evaluate_edge_operation, is still called from tests only. Five dead exports, not eight.

What survives, and it is the part that matters for Epic 4

geometry() (compiler.R:761) and evaluate_geometry() (:776) still accept no normalizer, transform or reducer; .run_geometry_compiler does not take them; .compiler_plan_id carries them as defaults only; and the receipt at compiler.R:690-699 is still a literal with .compile_effect_task having exactly one call site whose entire return is a digest. The effect-form receipt is still unfalsifiable and the plan is still discarded.

This correction HELPS Epic 4: measurement_form already demonstrates the target shape - a user-settable stage choice that changes stage_order in the receipt. Epic 4 can copy that pattern for the effect-form path and assert stage_order differences, rather than waiting on the Epic 0A decision. The 0A dependency therefore matters for the normalizer/transform axis only, not for the reducer axis.
